Chief_Complaint.content: Soreness and cracked skin of palms for 3–4 months, painful and itchy
Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: soreness/cracked skin of hands (palms) x 3–4 months; painful, itchy

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Soreness and cracked skin of hands (palms) for approximately 3–4 months
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: CC: soreness/cracked skin of hands (palms) x 3–4 months; painful, itchy

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Hand symptoms began approximately 3–4 months ago after job change
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: HPI: symptoms began ~3–4 months ago after job change

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Symptoms are worse in the palms
Hand rash bleeds when scratched sometimes
Hand symptoms are severe enough to impair work
Patient has been off work for the past 3 days due to hand symptoms
Patient works as a hotel housekeeper and uses bathroom cleaning products
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Occupational: hotel housekeeper; uses cleaning products (bathroom cleaners)

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient does not consistently wear gloves while using cleaning products
Patient tried E45 emollient without benefit
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Treatments tried: E45 emollient — no benefit

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient tried an oral antihistamine without benefit

Medications.content: Topical steroid cream prescribed for hand dermatitis
Medications.source_text: Topical steroid cream prescribed (as discussed) — prescription sent to pharmacy.

Medications.content: Stronger emollient prescribed or recommended for hands
Medications.source_text: Stronger emollient prescribed/recommended; apply/coating 3–4× daily for next couple weeks.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient drinks alcohol, a couple of pints per week

Assessment.content: Probable contact or irritant dermatitis of the palms, chronic for 3–4 months, associated with cleaning product exposure and inconsistent glove use, with pruritus, cracking, and occasional bleeding, causing work impairment
Assessment.source_text: 1. Probable contact/irritant dermatitis, palms — chronic (3–4 mo), associated with cleaning product exposure and inconsistent glove use; pruritus, cracking, occasional bleeding; causing work impairment.

Assessment.content: Type 2 diabetes is an active chronic condition treated with metformin
Assessment.source_text: 2. Type 2 diabetes — active chronic condition (on metformin).

Assessment.content: Work-related functional impairment with inability to work for 3 days
Assessment.source_text: 3. Work-related functional impairment (unable to work x3 days).

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient advised to avoid triggers by wearing protective gloves when cleaning and minimizing exposure to cleaning agents
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Avoid triggers: wear protective gloves when cleaning; minimize exposure to cleaning agents.

Plan_of_Care.content: Topical steroid cream prescribed and prescription sent to pharmacy
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Topical steroid cream prescribed (as discussed) — prescription sent to pharmacy.

Plan_of_Care.content: Stronger emollient prescribed or recommended to be applied 3–4 times daily for the next couple of weeks
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Stronger emollient prescribed/recommended; apply/coating 3–4× daily for next couple weeks.

Follow_up_Information.content: If no improvement in 1–2 weeks or if rash is spreading or worsening, patient should return sooner for review and further management
Follow_up_Information.source_text: • If no improvement in 1–2 weeks, or if spreading/worsening, return sooner for review and further management.
